subject: routing a task to the fast/cheap tier (Claude Haiku)

cases.scenario: A high-volume pipeline transcribes incoming webhook bodies into a fixed target schema — one cheap structured-output call per record, tens of thousands per day. The team is running them on the balanced tier and complaining about cost and latency.
cases.context: Mechanical slot-filling against a known schema; throughput and per-call cost dominate; no reasoning depth required.
cases.question: Where should this work run, and why?
expected_flags: Mechanical, high-volume slot-filling against a fixed schema is the fast tier's lane
Per-call cost and latency dominate at this volume, so the cheaper/faster tier is the right home
The balanced tier's reasoning is wasted here
expected_fix_hints: Route the transcription/slot-filling to the fast tier (claude-haiku)
Keep app-side validation; the model only fills the schema
absent_signals: Do not keep high-volume mechanical slot-filling on the balanced tier
Do not claim this work needs reasoning depth

cases.scenario: A task is mechanically trivial — extract a few fields from a single very large document — but the document is 600K tokens. The team plans to run it on the fast tier 'because the task is simple.'
cases.context: The task is simple but the input exceeds the fast tier's 200K context ceiling.
cases.question: Can the fast tier run this? Explain the boundary that applies.
expected_flags: The fast tier's 200K context ceiling is a STRUCTURAL limit — a 600K-token input cannot run on it regardless of how mechanical the task is
The context-size boundary is separate from the reasoning-difficulty boundary and must not be conflated
This forces escalation to a 1M-context tier even though the task needs no reasoning depth
expected_fix_hints: Escalate to a 1M-context tier (balanced or frontier) because the input exceeds 200K
Alternatively chunk the document so each call fits under 200K if that preserves correctness
absent_signals: Do not run a 600K-token input on the fast tier because the task 'looks simple'
Do not conflate the context ceiling with the reasoning-difficulty limit

cases.scenario: A small-looking task validates whether a financial discount calculation is correct before money moves. The team routes it to the fast tier 'because it's just a quick check.'
cases.context: The task is short but a wrong answer causes a financial miscalculation; correctness cost is high.
cases.question: Is the fast tier the right choice for this check? Justify.
expected_flags: A small-looking task with a high wrong-answer cost (money math) is the fast tier's trap case
The cost of a wrong answer outweighs the token saving, so this routes UP despite looking trivial
Cheapness is only safe inside the difficulty/correctness edges, not across them
expected_fix_hints: Route the financial-correctness check up to the balanced or frontier tier
Reserve the fast tier for low-stakes bounded judgment
absent_signals: Do not route high-correctness-cost money math to the fast tier to save tokens
Do not treat task size as a proxy for safe-to-cheapen

cases.scenario: A job does a fully deterministic bulk rename and find-and-replace across a directory with a known target string. The team routes it to the fast tier to keep it cheap.
cases.context: The transformation is fully deterministic and repeatable; no judgment of any kind is required.
cases.question: Is the fast tier the right executor? What is below it?
expected_flags: Fully deterministic, repeatable work belongs below any model — a script
The fast tier still costs tokens and latency for work a script does identically and exactly
The floor below the fast tier is 'no model at all'
expected_fix_hints: Use a deterministic script (sed/codemod) for the rename and replace
Reserve the fast tier for tasks needing a little judgment a regex cannot give
absent_signals: Do not route fully deterministic find-and-replace to any model when a script suffices
Do not treat the fast tier as the cheapest possible option when a script is cheaper and exact

cases.scenario: A task on the fast tier needs to dial up reasoning depth for a borderline-hard classification, and the engineer plans to pass an `effort: high` parameter to the fast-tier call.
cases.context: The decision rests on a capability fact: whether the fast tier supports the effort parameter.
cases.question: Will that work? What does it imply about the routing?
expected_flags: The fast tier does not support the effort parameter — there is no way to dial up reasoning depth on it
A task that needs tunable reasoning depth needs a higher tier by definition
The absence of the effort knob is itself a routing signal, not just a missing feature
expected_fix_hints: If the task genuinely needs more reasoning depth, escalate to a tier that supports effort
Verify the current effort-support fact live rather than assuming
absent_signals: Do not assume the fast tier accepts an effort parameter
Do not keep a reasoning-depth-dependent task on the fast tier

cases.scenario: During a provider overload (529 errors) on the busier tiers, a team needs to keep a batch of mechanical classification jobs flowing and asks whether the fast tier helps.
cases.context: The jobs are mechanical and low-stakes; the busier tiers are returning overload errors; the fast tier is often less loaded.
cases.question: Is the fast tier a reasonable fallback here? Any caveat?
expected_flags: The fast tier is often less loaded, making it a practical fallback during provider overload for mechanical work
It fits because the jobs are mechanical and low-stakes, not merely because it is available
High-volume ramps may hit the fast tier's separate rate-limit pool, which should be checked before scaling
expected_fix_hints: Use the fast tier as an overload fallback for the mechanical classification batch
Check the fast tier's rate-limit pool before scaling volume onto it
absent_signals: Do not move reasoning-heavy work to the fast tier just because the busier tiers are overloaded
Do not assume unlimited fast-tier capacity without checking its separate rate-limit pool

cases.scenario: A team asks how to design the polling loop and checkpoint topology their fast-tier status-checker runs inside, and how to write the API request that configures it — framing both as 'Haiku questions.'
cases.context: Loop topology and API call syntax are separate concerns from which model tier to pick; the team folds them under the Haiku label.
cases.question: How should the agent scope and route this request?
expected_flags: Designing the polling/checkpoint loop is loop architecture (autonomous-loop-patterns), not a model-tier decision
Writing the API request is call-site syntax (the claude-api reference), not the routing decision
Neither sub-question is answered by the fast-tier routing skill; both should be redirected
expected_fix_hints: Route the loop/checkpoint design to autonomous-loop-patterns
Route the API request syntax to the claude-api reference
absent_signals: Do not answer loop-topology design as if it were a model-tier choice
Do not write the API request syntax under the fast-tier routing skill's lane
